session_meta.research_objective:
Focus group guide exploring how men in the UK make everyday food
choices, how social context, work, hobbies, health, taste and other
people shape what they eat, how gender and masculinity may influence
food choices, and what would need to change for plant-based foods to
become more acceptable or appealing.
session_meta.topic_domain: Masculinity, food choice, animal product consumption, and plant-based eating
session_meta.participant_collective_identity: Men in the UK reflecting on food choices, male friendship, gender norms, and plant-based eating
session_meta.moderator_knowledge_brief:
Explore (1) everyday food decision-making, (2) the social contexts in
which men spend time with male friends, (3) the influence of other
people, work, hobbies, health, nutrition and taste on food choices,
(4) whether participants perceive gender as shaping what they eat,
(5) social acceptability and gendered meanings attached to vegetarian,
vegan, plant-based, feminine or masculine foods, and (6) what personal,
social and practical changes would make plant-based eating more viable
or appealing. The discussion should remain exploratory, non-judgmental,
and non-leading.

discussion_guide.scripted_question:
Hi everyone, thanks so much for joining the focus group today. We’re
going to take about 45 minutes to talk about your food choices and
opinions, and this will be recorded for research purposes. Try not to
overthink the questions, and simply speak freely. There are no right
or wrong answers. Please be respectful of your fellow focus group
members, and keep your responses relatively brief to allow time for
everyone to speak. But remember that this is a conversation, not an
interview, so you can jump in when you have something to say and you
don’t have to take turns answering each question, but you can if you
want to. Okay great, let’s start by going around and saying your name
and where in the UK you’re coming from today.

section_summaries.strategy_summary: The moderator's approach was scene-setting: establishing low-stakes norms (no right answers, conversational tone, brevity), then using a round-robin introduction to baseline the group geographically. Flagging the urban/rural spread before posing the first question was a light framing move, potentially priming participants to notice difference. It was functional but unremarkable — the real test of the approach begins with responses to the opening substantive prompt.

section_summaries.discussion_summary: This section established a clear urban/rural axis around social infrastructure: urban participants (Birmingham, Glasgow, Leeds, North East) converged on casual food and gym socialising as near-universal defaults, with local distinctiveness expressed through independent venues rather than chains. Will's rural experience — pub, house visits, outdoor activity, limited choice — emerged as the structural outlier, though he resisted framing this as deprivation. Ibrahim introduced a middle-ground register: urban infrastructure without the density of larger cities.
section_summaries.strategy_summary: The main move was letting urban participants establish consensus organically before surfacing Will as the counterpoint — David and Isaiah effectively did this work unprompted, which saved a moderator redirect. The brief intervention to hand Will the floor was necessary given the pile-on of curiosity. Correcting the London misattribution via Ibrahim's own clarification worked cleanly. The closing pivot to food decision-making was timely — the geographic mapping had reached saturation.

section_summaries.discussion_summary: This section centered on the distinction between preference and habit in meat eating, with participants splitting roughly between those who claim active preference (Ibrahim, Will) and those who acknowledge they cannot disentangle genuine taste from lifelong familiarity (Isaiah, Amir). David introduced a third position: deliberate indifference, alongside an unprompted rejection of meat-masculinity linkage. Social reinforcement through family and peer norms emerged as a connecting thread, setting up the gender question directly.
section_summaries.strategy_summary: The main moves were letting Will and Ibrahim's bilateral exchange run until it reached natural resolution, then widening to the group, and directly addressing David when he stayed quiet. David's volunteered gender remark was a gift — acknowledging it without chasing it immediately, then using it as the section's pivot point, felt like the right call. The transition into the gender question came from the content rather than the guide, which should make it land more naturally.
